comment: Dr. Norris is a great professor. His lectures are engaging, and his eccentric personality adds to them. His grading was pretty lenient in my opinion. He's open for office hours,  but it can be awkward sometimes, thats Dr Norris... very nice man overall who is there to support you, and if you get to know him, he's amazing. Would Recommend!!

Awesome professor, he was great at explaining difficult concepts and really cares about his students. Content was definitely tough but not anywhere as bad as orgo 2. One of my favorite science classes.
Just take him, he's great. Test corrections helped a lot!
You have test correction for exams. He is the most nicest professor I have ever met. He truly cares about every soul in his classroom, and very flexible and understanding.

Dr. Norris is an amazing professor. I have struggled in every chemistry class besides this one. He allows you to earn half credit back on assessments and emphasizes learning over scores. Definitely a lot of assessments, but he's clear about what's on them.He fosters an environment of collaboration and is incredibly accessible outside of class.

Emphasizes fully understanding the basis of content over memorizing it. Deeply enjoyed lectures & willingness to help struggling students. I'm never afraid to ask questions in order to clarify certain things. He is a bit particular when it comes to test responses, but it is because he truly cares and wants students to fully understand content.

Dr. Norris knows a lot about chemistry. I originally thought that his lectures were completely unorganized and unhelpful, but the truth is, that is kind of how inorganic chemistry is as a field. So, as long as you trust the process of the class, you'll end up fine, as his exams are not hard as long as you go to the review sessions.
One of the best if not the best

Amazing lectures, and you can tell that he's serious about the topic, and if you ask questions and go to office hours, you're more than likely to succeed. He's one of the best professors I have had so far, and if you're in his class you're very lucky.

Engaging, passionate, accessible.

Allows test corrections for half credit back, has 2-3 quizzams (not cumulative) and 2-3 examlets (cumulative). Hard class but achievable.

Slides could be more organized, have to take notes on the lecture because not all the notes are on the slides.

Dr. Norris is an absolutely fantastic professor!  He is the most accessible professor I've ever had.  Instead of scheduling office hours, he gives his schedule and allows students to show up whenever they're free.  He is very receptive to questions, and explains topics well both inside and out of class.

Dr. Norris is very approachable, he always answered his office hours and was willing to sit down (but never gave a straight answer) and the half point corrections really helped for exams. The class itself is hard so you're going to have to study on your own.

By far my favorite professor Ive had so far. I had this class at 8am and was dreading it, but he made it very engaging and it was never boring. Go to his office hours!! He is super helpful and will re teach info until you get it. Quizzes arent bad at all, exams are difficult (but fair) however you get to do test corrections to receive credit back

Dr. Norris is an excellent lecturer and a great guy who genuinely is interested in making sure his students understand the material. He gives quizzes that are worth 10 points (essentially negligible) to let you know what you need to study. His tests are incredibly difficult imo but extremely rewarding if you can do effective problem deduction.

Dr. Norris is one of the best profs I've ever seen in UR. He tries his best to help everyone. Personally, I ask a lot of questions.. and he answers all of them, without hating me, lmao hopefully. If you are actually interested in learning chem, he is always going to help you. Quizzes are on Fridays, tests are hard. BUT attend the classes!

Easily one of the best professors I have had as I understand chemistry on a whole new level now! He had a great office hour schedule and these one-on-one meetings were super helpful (he would happily re-explain concepts or lectures if needed). This class required a LOT of time and effort but was so worth it. He's great!
This class is very hard and professor norris is not the best lecturer. He is very good one on one however in class it is hard. You can get back half of the points on your test.

I love Dr. Norris! He has a nerdy sense of humor and tries his best to make class interactive and fun. He's new, so his ability to command a classroom is not that of a seasoned professor, but he was still good at explaining concepts and his tests were very fair and straightforward. He is also receptive to feedback and allows for test corrections.

Norris was excellent. Extremely helpful and patient. office almost always opened. Doesnt give extra credit, but allows for test corrections. Tries to give as many points as possible. Course extremely hard because its fast and covers a load of material. Luckily he used various ways to engage his students; to get point across. doughnuts and bagels

Great guy, always looking for new ways to engage his students in learning. Cares about his students and wants to make sure they understand concepts. Tests are challenging but corrections can help improve those grades.

He's brand new to teaching and you can tell, because he's not great at explaining things. Though he clearly states concepts he doesn't emphasize what is most important, which makes studying for tests hard. He seems to curve exam scores instead of trying different ways to teach more effectively, which is good for my grade but not future chem classes
